title: Anthoceros agrestis (hornwort) transformation protocol
author: Eftychis Frangedakis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6izhcf6

steps.title: Collect and homogenize thallus tissue
steps.instruction: Collect approximately 2 g of thallus tissue grown for 4 weeks under low light (≈0.1 g per petri dish, 20 dishes). Split the tissue into three parts, place each part in a 50 mL Falcon tube with 15 mL sterile water, and homogenize for 5 seconds at the lowest power setting (8000 rpm). Transfer the homogenate from one tube through a 100 µm cell strainer, wash the strainer with 50 mL sterile water, and dispense the filtrate onto two petri dishes (six plates total) containing solid KNOP medium; add 2–3 mL sterile water to each plate. Incubate at 21 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark, light intensity 3–5 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Second homogenization and short culture
steps.instruction: After 3–4 weeks, transfer the tissue from the petri dishes into a Falcon tube using sterile scalpels. Re‑homogenize the tissue in 15–20 mL sterile water, filter through a 100 µm cell strainer, and spread the filtrate onto four petri dishes containing solid KNOP medium (add 2 mL sterile water if needed to aid spreading). Grow for 2 days at 21 °C under continuous light (or 12 h light/12 h dark) with light intensity 30 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium preculture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL LB medium with a single AGL1 Agrobacterium colony, 10 µg/mL rifampicin, 50 µg/mL carbenicillin, and the plasmid‑specific selection antibiotic. Incubate at 28 °C for 2 days with shaking at 120 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare infection suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 5 mL of the 2‑day Agrobacterium culture (OD 2.5–2.7) for 7 minutes at 1800 × g. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL liquid KNOP medium containing 2 % (w/v) sucrose and 100 µM acetosyringone. Incubate the suspension with shaking at 120 rpm, 28 °C for 5 hours.

steps.title: Co‑cultivate tissue with Agrobacterium
steps.instruction: Co‑cultivation of regenerated thallus with Agrobacterium.

substeps.instruction: Wash the regenerating thallus through a 100 µm cell strainer.
Transfer half of the tissue from one plate into a single well of a 6‑well plate containing 4 mL liquid KNOP medium supplemented with 2 % (w/v) sucrose.
Add 80 µL of the prepared Agrobacterium suspension and 100 µM acetosyringone to achieve a final acetosyringone concentration of 100 µM.
Incubate for 3 days with shaking at 110 rpm, 21 °C, under ambient room light (1–3 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹).

steps.title: First selection on antibiotics
steps.instruction: Using a sterile plastic pipette, transfer the tissue from the well into a 100 µm cell strainer, drain, and place onto solid KNOP plates containing 100 µg/mL cefotaxime and 10 µg/mL hygromycin. Add 2 mL sterile water to each plate to facilitate spreading. Incubate at 21 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark, light intensity 35 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Second selection on antibiotics
steps.instruction: After 3 weeks, transfer the tissue to fresh solid KNOP medium containing 100 µg/mL cefotaxime and 10 µg/mL hygromycin; add 2 mL sterile water to each plate. Grow at 21 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark, light intensity 35 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Third selection on antibiotics
steps.instruction: Transfer surviving tissue fragments onto solid KNOP medium containing 100 µg/mL cefotaxime and 10 µg/mL hygromycin. Grow at 21 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark, light intensity 3–35 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
